test_title: SSC CGL Tier 2 Quant Previous Year Paper (Held On: 8 Aug 2022)
subject: general
question:
A alone can do a work in 11 days. B alone can do the same work in 22 days. C alone can do the same work in 33 days.

They work in the following manner :

Day 1: A and B work.

Day 2: B and C work.

Day 3: C and A work.

Day 4: A and B work. And so on.

In how many days will the work be completed ?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Total Work = LCM(11, 22, 33) = 66 units.

Efficiencies: A = 6, B = 3, C = 2 units/day.

Work in 1 cycle (3 days): (A+B) + (B+C) + (C+A) = (6+3) + (3+2) + (2+6) = 22 units.

Total cycles needed = Total Work ÷ Work per cycle = 66 ÷ 22 = 3 cycles.

Total days = 3 cycles × 3 days/cycle = 9 days.

**∴ The correct answer is 9 days.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

Given:

Time taken by A = 11 days

Time taken by B = 22 days

Time taken by C = 33 days

Formula used: Efficiency = Total Work ÷ Time

Calculations:

⇒ Day 1 Work (A + B) = 6 + 3 = 9 units

⇒ Day 2 Work (B + C) = 3 + 2 = 5 units

⇒ Day 3 Work (C + A) = 2 + 6 = 8 units

⇒ Total work done in 3 days (1 cycle) = 9 + 5 + 8 = 22 units

⇒ Total work to be completed = 66 units

⇒ Number of cycles = 66 ÷ 22 = 3 cycles

⇒ Total time = 3 × 3 = 9 days

**∴ The correct answer is 9 days.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Alternate Day Work

In problems where work is done on alternate days or in a specific cyclic pattern, calculate the total work done in one complete cycle first and then divide the total work by the cycle sum.

Work and Wages

Wages are always distributed in the ratio of the actual work done by each individual, which is proportional to their Efficiency × Time.

Pipes and Cisterns

This concept is identical to Time and Work, where an outlet pipe has negative efficiency (emptying work) and an inlet pipe has positive efficiency (filling work).</p
